html:
The Battle of Boyacá was fought on 7 August 1819 at a bridge in the highlands of Colombia. The patriot army of Simón Bolívar and Francisco de Paula Santander defeated the Spanish and won the independence of New Granada.

Bolívar had led his army, with British volunteers and llanero horsemen, from the plains of Venezuela over the frozen Andes, a march that cost many lives. They surprised the royalists, who were trying to reach Bogotá. Santander's vanguard took the bridge, and the Spanish army surrendered in about two hours.

Three days later Bolívar entered Bogotá, and the viceroy fled. In December the republic of Gran Colombia was proclaimed. Boyacá is the founding battle of Colombia, and 7 August is a national holiday. Santander became its vice-president.
